proofs.proof_tex:
Because \(p^z\) is a conditional probability vector and \(0<\rho<1\),
\[
 p^z_{xy}\geq 0,
 \qquad
 \sum_{x\in\mathcal E}\sum_{y=0}^1p^z_{xy}=1,
 \qquad z\in\{0,1\}.
 \tag{1}
\]
Compatibility means that \(\mathcal Q_T(p)\neq\varnothing\).  The sharp-envelope theorem therefore applies and gives
\[
 \{\theta_{ab}(q):q\in\mathcal Q_T(p)\}
 =[L_T(p),U_T(p)],
 \quad
 L_T(p)=\max_{f\in\mathfrak F^-_T}f(p),
 \quad
 U_T(p)=\min_{f\in\mathfrak F^+_T}f(p).
 \tag{2}
\]

Suppose first that \(T=\{a,b\}\).  The index set \(T\setminus\{a,b\}\) is empty.  Thus the definition of the two-diagonal capacity gives
\[
 D_T(p)
 =\min\bigl(\{u+v\}\cup\varnothing\bigr)
 =u+v.
 \tag{3}
\]
The affine-list definition and (2) consequently give
\[
 L_T(p)=\max_{1\leq j\leq8}\ell_j(p),
 \qquad
 U_T(p)=\min_{1\leq j\leq8}\{-\ell_j(\bar p)\}.
 \tag{4}
\]
Every quantity on the right side of (4) is a function only of
\[
 \alpha_z=p^z_{a0},\quad \gamma_z=p^z_{a1},\quad
 \delta_z=p^z_{b0},\quad \beta_z=p^z_{b1},
 \qquad z\in\{0,1\}.
 \tag{5}
\]

If \(\mathcal E=\{a,b\}\), the observed exposure itself is binary.  Relabeling the two exposure values as \(0=a\) and \(1=b\), and using (5), term-by-term substitution in the definition of \(\ell_1,\ldots,\ell_8\) gives the eight Balke--Pearl lower expressions; substituting \(\bar p^z_{xy}=p^z_{x,1-y}\) gives their eight upper expressions as \(-\ell_j(\bar p)\).  The cited Balke--Pearl result states that the maximum and minimum of those respective lists are the sharp binary average-effect endpoints.  Combining that result with (2)--(5) proves the first reduction.  Notice that this is the only case in which the observed exposure alphabet is literally binary.

Now retain \(T=\{a,b\}\) but suppose \(U\neq\varnothing\), and define \(p^{\rm m}\) as in the statement.  Equation (1) shows that \(p^{{\rm m},z}\) is a probability vector.  It is also compatible with the three-category selected-trust model.  Indeed, choose any \(q\in\mathcal Q_T(p)\), put
\[
 X_z^{\rm m}=\begin{cases}
 X_z,&X_z\in\{a,b\},\\
 c^\dagger,&X_z\in U,
 \end{cases}
 \qquad V_a^{\rm m}=V_a,qquad V_b^{\rm m}=V_b,
 \tag{6}
\]
and, on the event \(X_z\in U\), set \(W^{\rm m}_{c^\dagger z}=W_{X_z z}\), assigning this binary slot arbitrarily off that event.  The events \(\{X_z=x\}\), \(x\in U\), are disjoint, so the compatible-response-law equations imply
\[
 \Pr(X_z^{\rm m}=c^\dagger,W^{\rm m}_{c^\dagger z}=y)
 =\sum_{x\in U}\Pr_q(X_z=x,W_{xz}=y)
 =\sum_{x\in U}p^z_{xy}
 =p^{{\rm m},z}_{c^\dagger y}.
 \tag{7}
\]
For \(x\in\{a,b\}\), (6) instead yields
\[
 \Pr(X_z^{\rm m}=x,V_x^{\rm m}=y)
 =\Pr_q(X_z=x,V_x=y)
 =p^z_{xy}
 =p^{{\rm m},z}_{xy}.
 \tag{8}
\]
Equations (7)--(8) prove compatibility of \(p^{\rm m}\) from the definition of \(\mathcal Q_{\{a,b\}}(p^{\rm m})\).

The four target-cell vectors in (5) are unchanged by merging.  Hence every term on the right side of (4), both for \(p\) and for its outcome reversal, is unchanged:
\[
 \ell_j(p^{\rm m})=\ell_j(p),
 \qquad
 \ell_j(\overline{p^{\rm m}})=\ell_j(\bar p),
 \qquad 1\leq j\leq8.
 \tag{9}
\]
Applying (2)--(4) to both compatible tables and using (9) proves equality of their sharp intervals.  Gabriel--Sachs--Sjolander Result 1 states that, with a binary instrument, two well-defining target exposure levels, and one merged potentially ill-defining level, these same first eight lower and upper expressions are sharp.  Thus this reduction is to their Result 1, rather than a claim that the original arbitrary-support observed exposure is binary.

For the ternary full-trust case, write \(\mathcal E=\{a,b,c\}\) and \(T=\mathcal E\).  There is exactly one trusted nuisance category.  From the definitions of \(\kappa\), \(h\), and \(C^-\),
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 C^-_{c,y}(p)
 &=\kappa-h_{cy}\\
 &=-2+\alpha_0+\alpha_1+\beta_0+\beta_1
      +p^0_{cy}+p^1_{c,1-y},
 \qquad y\in\{0,1\}.
 \end{aligned}
 \tag{10}
\]
Likewise, because \(C^+_{c,y}(p)=-C^-_{c,1-y}(\bar p)\),
\[
 C^+_{c,y}(p)
 =2-\gamma_0-\gamma_1-\delta_0-\delta_1
     -p^0_{cy}-p^1_{c,1-y},
 \qquad y\in\{0,1\}.
 \tag{11}
\]
The affine-list definition therefore supplies exactly eight baseline expressions plus the two expressions in (10) for the lower endpoint, and eight outcome-reversed baseline expressions plus the two expressions in (11) for the upper endpoint.  Under the relabeling \(x=a\), \(x'=b\), and \(x''=c\), direct substitution of \(p_{xy\cdot z}=p^z_{xy}\) shows that (10) and (11) are respectively the final two lines of Gabriel--Sachs--Sjolander equations (3) and (4), while the definitions of \(\ell_1,\ldots,\ell_8\) give their first eight lines.  Their cited ternary result establishes that those ten-term maxima and minima are sharp.  Together with (2), this proves the third reduction.

Finally suppose \(T=\mathcal E\).  Then \(U=\varnothing\), and the response space and observation equations reduce to
\[
 \mathcal R_T=\mathcal E^2\times\{0,1\}^{\mathcal E},
 \qquad R=(X_0,X_1,V),
 \qquad X=X_Z,
 \qquad Y=V_X.
 \tag{12}
\]
For any \(q\in\mathcal Q_T(p)\), draw \(Z\) independently of \(R\), as required by random assignment and the mixed-trust observation map.  Equations (12) and the definition of compatibility then give
\[
 \Pr_q(X_z=x,V_x=y)=p^z_{xy},
 \qquad x\in\mathcal E,quad y,z\in\{0,1\}.
 \tag{13}
\]
Thus \((X_0,X_1,V)\), together with the independent instrument, is a law in Song--Guo--Chan--Richardson model \(\mathcal M_1\): it has exposure responses for both instrument values, a single outcome response \(V_x\) for every exposure value, individual-level exclusion, consistency, and random assignment.

Conversely, take a law in their \(\mathcal M_1\), restricted to binary \(Z,Y\) and exposure alphabet \(\mathcal E\).  Its marginal law of the complete response vector \((X(0),X(1),(Y(x):x\in\mathcal E))\) defines a \(q\) on the space in (12).  Individual-level exclusion and consistency identify \(Y=Y(X)=V_X\), while random assignment and \(0<\rho<1\) imply
\[
 \Pr_q(X_z=x,V_x=y)
 =\Pr(X=x,Y=y\mid Z=z)
 =p^z_{xy}.
 \tag{14}
\]
Hence \(q\in\mathcal Q_T(p)\).  Equations (13)--(14) prove equality, at every fixed \(p\), between the attainable joint laws of \(V\) in the full-trust model here and the corresponding fiber of the image of \(\mathcal M_1\).

The cited equal-image theorem of Song--Guo--Chan--Richardson states that the image pairs consisting of the joint potential-outcome law and the observed conditional law are identical for \(\mathcal M_1,\ldots,\mathcal M_5\).  Let \(\phi\) denote their image map and, for \(i\in\{1,\ldots,5\}\), define its fiber at the observed table by
\[
 \Phi_i(p)=\{\mu:(\mu,p)\in\phi(\mathcal M_i)\},
 \tag{15}
\]
where \(\mu\) is a probability mass function on \(\{0,1\}^{\mathcal E}\).  Equality of the pair images gives, by taking the section with second coordinate \(p\),
\[
 \Phi_1(p)=\Phi_2(p)=\cdots=\Phi_5(p).
 \tag{16}
\]
Define the linear functional
\[
 \tau_{ab}(\mu)=\sum_{v\in\{0,1\}^{\mathcal E}}(v_b-v_a)\mu(v).
 \tag{17}
\]
This functional depends only on the joint potential-outcome law.  Applying \(\tau_{ab}\) to the equal fibers in (16), and applying the sharp-envelope theorem to the \(\mathcal M_1\) fiber via (12)--(14), gives, for every \(i\in\{1,\ldots,5\}\),
\[
 \{\tau_{ab}(\mu):\mu\in\Phi_i(p)\}
 =[L_T(p),U_T(p)]
 \tag{18}
\]
because \(\tau_{ab}(\operatorname{Law}_q(V))=\mathbb E_q[V_b-V_a]=\theta_{ab}(q)\).  This proves the last claim.

added_lemmas.statement: For a binary instrument, binary exposure, and binary outcome under random assignment, individual-level exclusion, and consistency, Balke and Pearl's displayed average-causal-effect bounds are sharp and consist of a lower endpoint equal to the maximum of eight affine observed-cell expressions and an upper endpoint equal to the minimum of eight affine observed-cell expressions.

source.locator: Displayed sharp bounds on the average causal effect in the binary response-function model

proposed_statement_changes.proposed:
For every compatible observed table \(p\), the following comparator reductions hold.  First, if \(\mathcal E=\{a,b\}\), then necessarily \(T=\mathcal E\), \(D_T(p)=u+v\), and \([L_T(p),U_T(p)]\) is literally the sharp Balke--Pearl interval for the binary exposure contrast \(\mathbb E[V_b-V_a]\).  Second, suppose \(T=\{a,b\}\) and \(U\neq\varnothing\).  Introduce a new label \(c^\dagger\) and form the three-category table
\[
 p^{{\rm m},z}_{ay}=p^z_{ay},\qquad
 p^{{\rm m},z}_{by}=p^z_{by},\qquad
 p^{{\rm m},z}_{c^\dagger y}=\sum_{x\in U}p^z_{xy}.
\]
Then \([L_T(p),U_T(p)]\) equals the eight-piece sharp interval computed from \(p^{\rm m}\), which is the setting and conclusion of Gabriel--Sachs--Sjolander Result 1: two trusted target levels and one merged wholly untrusted remainder.  Third, if \(\mathcal E=\{a,b,c\}\) and \(T=\mathcal E\), then the lower list consists of \(\ell_1,\ldots,\ell_8,C^-_{c,0},C^-_{c,1}\), the upper list consists of their outcome-reversed negatives, and these are exactly the ten lower and ten upper expressions in Gabriel--Sachs--Sjolander equations (3)--(4).  Finally, for arbitrary finite \(\mathcal E\) under full trust \(T=\mathcal E\), the image of the response-law model in pairs consisting of the joint law of \(V\) and the observed table \(p\) is the image of Song--Guo--Chan--Richardson model \(\mathcal M_1\), restricted to binary \(Z\) and \(Y\).  Hence its \(\theta_{ab}\)-projection is \([L_T(p),U_T(p)]\); by their equal-image theorem, exactly the same interval is the \(\theta_{ab}\)-projection under each of their models \(\mathcal M_2,\ldots,\mathcal M_5\).
proposed_statement_changes.reason: The current first clause calls an arbitrary-support selected-trust table a Balke--Pearl binary-exposure model. Literal Balke--Pearl equivalence requires a two-category exposure; with additional wholly untrusted categories the faithful comparator is Gabriel--Sachs--Sjolander Result 1 after merging the remainder. The replacement also states the exact Song model-image transfer required by the directive.

proposed.justification: The proposition certifies exact comparator fidelity: literal binary equivalence, the merged-untrusted Gabriel reduction, the fully trusted ternary ten-term reduction, and the full-trust Song image transfer.
proposed.gap: The published results occupy different model scopes; the missing step is to prove which specialization or push-forward of the selected-trust model lands in each scope without conflating them.
proposed.consumer: Existing binary and ternary implementations can use the first three identities as regression tests, while analysts using alternative categorical-IV formulations can use the Song equal-image transfer.

proposed_core_edits.reason: The narrowed comparator claim needs the observation-map definitions, randomization and positivity conditions, and four source-level cited leaves added to its declared proof spine; its note metadata is synchronized with the corrected scope.

proposed.comparator_claim: For binary instrument, exposure, and outcome, the sharp average-effect interval is the maximum and minimum of eight affine response-function expressions.
Result 1 gives the classical eight-piece bounds for two well-defining target levels plus one merged potentially ill-defining remainder.
Equations (3)--(4) give ten sharp lower and upper expressions for a binary instrument and three well-defining exposure levels.
Theorem 1 gives the same joint potential-outcome and observed-law image for the five categorical instrumental-variable models in Table 2.
The five full-category models have the same observed-law image, which excludes some laws admitted when exclusion is imposed only on selected categories.
Theorem 17 characterizes the observable binary-instrument, binary-outcome, arbitrary-exposure model under full exclusion by instrumental inequalities.
For a finite response-function class, dual vertex enumeration yields valid and tight symbolic bounds for linear causal queries.
A multinomial Kullback--Leibler confidence region gives simultaneous finite-sample coverage for linear functionals of the fully valid categorical-IV counterfactual law.
Identification gains for binary average-effect bounds can be decomposed into contributions from instrument information and model features.

proposed_core_edits.reason: The corrected positioning separates literal Balke--Pearl equivalence, Gabriel's merged-remainder and ternary results, Song's equal-image transfer, and the Bhadane observed-model obstruction instead of assigning all full-exclusion claims to one comparator theorem.

prose_updates.tldr: With a randomized binary instrument, binary outcome, and arbitrary finite categorical exposure, exclusion and consistency may be credible only on a declared trusted subset containing the two target categories. The sharp pairwise-effect interval is governed by one two-diagonal capacity: each endpoint evaluates eight baseline affine pieces and exactly two pieces per trusted nuisance category, with finite laws attaining both endpoints. Trust is nested by an explicit response-law restriction map, and separate positive-cell witnesses show strict observed-law enlargement from selected trust and strict identified-set tightening from adding trust. Comparator scope is exact: Balke--Pearl is recovered literally only for a binary exposure; a merged wholly untrusted remainder is Gabriel--Sachs--Sjolander Result 1; full trust with three categories gives their ten terms; and arbitrary finite full trust is Song--Guo--Chan--Richardson model M1, with the pairwise interval transferring to models M2 through M5 by their equal-image theorem. Finite-sample whole-set coverage remains valid at ties and zero cells.

project_justification.gap: Balke and Pearl give the literal binary-exposure envelope. Gabriel, Sachs, and Sjolander give both the two-target result with one merged wholly untrusted remainder and the ten-term fully trusted ternary formulas. Song, Guo, Chan, and Richardson characterize arbitrary finite categorical exposure under full trust and prove that five IV formulations have the same joint potential-outcome and observed-law image, but leave scalar pairwise endpoints to generic optimization. What is missing is an arbitrary-finite sharp scalar envelope when trust is category selective, together with an exact nesting map and strict witnesses on the common observed-law domain.
project_justification.niche: Applied adherence studies often have two interventionally meaningful target categories, several intermediate categories for which exclusion may be separately defensible, and residual categories for which no cross-instrument outcome equality is credible. That structure is neither a binary exposure model nor a fully exclusion-valid categorical model.
project_justification.fill: The two-diagonal transport reduction supplies the sharp linear-size envelope and finite endpoint laws for the mixed-trust model. The response-law restriction map proves that enlarging trust nests both compatibility classes and identified sets; the separation and gain tables make both inclusions strict in the appropriate sense. Exact reductions recover Balke--Pearl only on a genuinely binary alphabet, Gabriel's merged-remainder and ternary formulas in their stated scopes, and Song's five equal images under arbitrary finite full trust.

prose_updates.related_work: Balke and Pearl derive eight sharp affine average-effect expressions for binary instrument, binary exposure, and binary outcome; the present formula is called literally Balke--Pearl only when the exposure alphabet has two elements. Gabriel, Sachs, and Sjolander Result 1 treats two well-defining target levels plus one merged potentially ill-defining remainder and recovers those eight expressions, while their equations (3)--(4) give ten sharp expressions per endpoint for three well-defining exposure levels. These are the faithful published reductions of the selected-trust formula. Sachs, Jonzon, Sjolander, and Gabriel provide general symbolic primal--dual machinery for finite response-function models; that machinery informs certification but is not the linear-size envelope proved here. Song, Guo, Chan, and Richardson characterize arbitrary categorical IV models under full trust. Their model M1 coincides with this paper's full-trust response-law image, and their Theorem 1 proves equality of the joint potential-outcome and observed-law images of models M1 through M5, so the sharp pairwise interval transfers exactly to all five formulations. Bhadane, Mooij, Boeken, and Zoeter Theorem 17 gives the observed full-exclusion compatibility characterization for binary instrument and outcome with arbitrary finite exposure. The cell-sum inequality violated by the separation family is attributed to that observed-model result and also follows directly because the two relevant full-exclusion factual events are disjoint. That family is selected-trust compatible on a positive-cell neighborhood but not full-trust representable, whereas the separate full-trust-compatible gain table shows strict identified-set tightening after trusting the intermediate category. VanderWeele and Hernan explain why coarse labels may hide treatment versions, and Marshall studies bias from coarsening; they motivate the distinction between a trusted refinement and a wholly untrusted split or merge. Zhang, Frazier, Poskitt, and Zhao analyze identification gains for binary average-effect bounds; the categorywise active-face update here is a corollary of the sharp envelope. Du Toit and collaborators supply the LEAP adherence application in which separately justified intermediate consumption categories may or may not change the low-versus-high interval.

statement_notes.justification: The proposition prevents comparator drift by proving the exact push-forward, relabeling, and model-image identities that connect the selected-trust envelope to each published result.
statement_notes.gap: The nearest results use different exposure alphabets and exclusion scopes; a literal binary claim for an arbitrary-support table or an unqualified appeal to the full-trust categorical model would be false.
statement_notes.consumer: Binary and ternary software can use the exact identities as regression tests, and full-trust analyses formulated under any of Song's five models inherit the same pairwise interval.

proofs.proof_tex:
For a trusted set \(S\) containing \(a\) and \(b\), define the observable-model image and the identified set, respectively, by
\[
 \mathcal P_S=\{p:\mathcal Q_S(p)\neq\varnothing\},
 \qquad
 \Theta_S(p)=\{\theta_{ab}(q):q\in\mathcal Q_S(p)\}.
\]
We first record the relevant nesting by an explicit restriction-map argument.  If \(S\subseteq S'\) and \(q'\in\mathcal Q_{S'}(p)\), push \(q'\) forward as follows: retain \(X_0,X_1\), retain \((V_x:x\in S)\), set
\[
 W_{xz}=V_x\quad(x\in S'\setminus S,\ z\in\{0,1\}),
\]
and retain the existing \(W_{xz}\) slots for \(x\in\mathcal E\setminus S'\).  For \(x\in S\), the defining probabilities \(\Pr(X_z=x,V_x=y)\) are unchanged.  For \(x\in S'\setminus S\),
\[
 \Pr(X_z=x,W_{xz}=y)=\Pr(X_z=x,V_x=y)=p^z_{xy},
\]
and the same equality is unchanged for \(x\in\mathcal E\setminus S'\).  Thus the definition of compatible response laws gives a law \(q\in\mathcal Q_S(p)\).  Because \(a,b\in S\), the map retains \(V_a,V_b\), whence
\[
 \theta_{ab}(q)=\mathbb E_q[V_b-V_a]
 =\mathbb E_{q'}[V_b-V_a]=\theta_{ab}(q').
\]
This finite pushforward construction proves
\[
 \mathcal P_{S'}\subseteq\mathcal P_S,
 \qquad
 \Theta_{S'}(p)\subseteq\Theta_S(p)\quad(p\in\mathcal P_{S'}).
 \tag{1}
\]

We next use the explicit response-law witness.  Its allocation probability is \(\rho=1/2\), so both instrument arms have positive probability.  Under \(q^{\rm sep}_{r,s,\tau,\lambda}\), the independence stipulated in the witness construction and the mixed-trust observation map give, for \(z\in\{0,1\}\),
\[
\begin{aligned}
 \Pr(X_z=a,V_a=0)&=A_z(1-\tau_a),&
 \Pr(X_z=a,V_a=1)&=A_z\tau_a,\\
 \Pr(X_z=b,V_b=0)&=B_z(1-\tau_b),&
 \Pr(X_z=b,V_b=1)&=B_z\tau_b,\\
 \Pr(X_z=c_\star,W_{c_\star z}=0)&=r_z(1-\lambda_z),&
 \Pr(X_z=c_\star,W_{c_\star z}=1)&=r_z\lambda_z.
\end{aligned}
\tag{2}
\]
These are exactly the displayed cells of \(p^{\rm sep}\).  Since \(c_\star\) is untrusted under \(T_0\), (2) satisfies every equality in the definition of \(\mathcal Q_{T_0}(p^{\rm sep})\).  Hence
\[
 q^{\rm sep}_{r,s,\tau,\lambda}\in\mathcal Q_{T_0}(p^{\rm sep}),
 \qquad p^{\rm sep}\in\mathcal P_{T_0}.
 \tag{3}
\]

The parameter ranges imply
\[
 1-r_z>\frac8{25},
 \qquad s_z,1-s_z,\tau_x,1-\tau_x>\frac25
 \quad(x\in\{a,b\}).
\]
Therefore each target-category cell in (2) is larger than
\[
 \frac8{25}\left(\frac25\right)^2
 =\frac{32}{625}>\frac{93}{5000}.
 \tag{4}
\]
For the two smaller nuisance cells,
\[
 r_0\lambda_0>\frac{31}{50}\frac3{100}=\frac{93}{5000},
 \qquad
 r_1(1-\lambda_1)>\frac{31}{50}\frac3{100}=\frac{93}{5000}.
 \tag{5}
\]
The other two nuisance cells exceed \((31/50)(93/100)\), because \(1-\lambda_0>93/100\) and \(\lambda_1>93/100\).  Equations (4)--(5) prove that every observed cell is strictly larger than \(93/5000\).

For \(x=a\), its exposure mass is \(A_z\), and for \(x=b\), its exposure mass is \(B_z\).  Since \(1-r_z<19/50\) and both \(s_z\) and \(1-s_z\) are smaller than \(3/5\),
\[
 A_z<\frac{57}{250},
 \qquad B_z<\frac{57}{250}.
\]
Every cell is bounded above by its category mass, so, for \(x\in\{a,b\}\) and \(y\in\{0,1\}\),
\[
 p^{{\rm sep},0}_{xy}+p^{{\rm sep},1}_{x,1-y}
 <2\frac{57}{250}=\frac{57}{125}.
 \tag{6}
\]

We now give a direct disjoint-event certificate for failure of full trust.  Under any law in \(\mathcal Q_{T_1}(p)\), the events
\[
 \mathcal A_0=\{X_0=c_\star,V_{c_\star}=0\},
 \qquad
 \mathcal A_1=\{X_1=c_\star,V_{c_\star}=1\}
\]
are disjoint, because the same binary variable \(V_{c_\star}\) cannot equal both zero and one.  The compatibility equalities therefore imply the necessary inequality
\[
 p^0_{c_\star0}+p^1_{c_\star1}
 =\Pr(\mathcal A_0)+\Pr(\mathcal A_1)
 =\Pr(\mathcal A_0\cup\mathcal A_1)\leq1.
 \tag{7}
\]
For the separation table, however,
\[
\begin{aligned}
 p^{{\rm sep},0}_{c_\star0}+p^{{\rm sep},1}_{c_\star1}
 &=r_0(1-\lambda_0)+r_1\lambda_1\\
 &>2\frac{31}{50}\frac{93}{100}
 =\frac{2883}{2500}>1.
\end{aligned}
\tag{8}
\]
Thus \(p^{\rm sep}\notin\mathcal P_{T_1}\).  Together with (1) and (3), this proves strict observed-law inclusion \(\mathcal P_{T_1}\subsetneq\mathcal P_{T_0}\).

This separation is perturbation-stable.  Let \(p'\) be armwise normalized and satisfy
\(\lVert p'-p^{\rm sep}\rVert_\infty<1/200\).  By (4)--(5), every cell of \(p'\) is larger than
\[
 \frac{93}{5000}-\frac1{200}=\frac{68}{5000}>0.
 \tag{9}
\]
By (6), for every \(x\in\{a,b\}\) and \(y\in\{0,1\}\),
\[
 p'^0_{xy}+p'^1_{x,1-y}
 <\frac{57}{125}+\frac2{200}<1.
 \tag{10}
\]
Armwise normalization, nonnegativity from (9), and (10) satisfy the necessary and sufficient conditions in \(\mathrm{lem{:}compatibility}\), so \(p'\in\mathcal P_{T_0}\).  Conversely, (8) gives
\[
 p'^0_{c_\star0}+p'^1_{c_\star1}
 >\frac{2883}{2500}-\frac2{200}>1,
\]
which violates the direct necessary condition (7); hence \(p'\notin\mathcal P_{T_1}\).  This proves the asserted positive-radius obstruction in the affine space of armwise normalized tables.

It remains to prove a strict identified-set gain on the common domain.  The two arms of \(p^{\rm gain}\) are normalized and all twelve cells are positive.  For categories \(a\) and \(b\), every compatibility sum is \(1/5\).  For \(c_\star\), the two sums are
\[
 p^{{\rm gain},0}_{c_\star0}+p^{{\rm gain},1}_{c_\star1}=\frac9{10},
 \qquad
 p^{{\rm gain},0}_{c_\star1}+p^{{\rm gain},1}_{c_\star0}=\frac3{10}.
 \tag{11}
\]
All nonnegativity and compatibility inequalities are strict.  The compatibility lemma therefore gives \(p^{\rm gain}\in\mathcal P_{T_1}\), and the strict inequalities exhibit a relative neighborhood, within the arm-normalization affine space, contained in \(\mathcal P_{T_1}\).  Thus \(p^{\rm gain}\) is in the relative interior of the full-trust compatible set.  By (1), it also belongs to \(\mathcal P_{T_0}\).

At this table, the target cells give
\[
 \alpha_0=\alpha_1=\beta_0=\beta_1
 =\gamma_0=\gamma_1=\delta_0=\delta_1=\frac1{10},
 \qquad \kappa=-\frac35.
\]
The two individual diagonal caps are \(u=v=1/10\).  Hence the endpoint formula in \(\mathrm{thm{:}sharp-envelope}\) yields
\[
 D_{T_0}(p^{\rm gain})=u+v=\frac15,
 \qquad
 L_{T_0}(p^{\rm gain})=-\frac35-\frac15=-\frac45.
 \tag{12}
\]
Outcome reversal leaves all target cells unchanged, so
\[
 U_{T_0}(p^{\rm gain})=-L_{T_0}(\bar p^{\rm gain})=\frac45.
 \tag{13}
\]
Under \(T_1\), the nuisance caps are
\[
 h_{c_\star0}=1-\frac5{10}-\frac4{10}=\frac1{10},
 \qquad
 h_{c_\star1}=1-\frac1{10}-\frac2{10}=\frac7{10}.
\]
Consequently,
\[
 D_{T_1}(p^{\rm gain})
 =\min\left\{\frac15,\frac1{10},\frac7{10}\right\}=\frac1{10},
 \qquad
 L_{T_1}(p^{\rm gain})=-\frac7{10}.
 \tag{14}
\]
Outcome reversal interchanges the two nuisance caps and leaves the remaining quantities unchanged; hence \(U_{T_1}(p^{\rm gain})=7/10\).  Applying the sharp-envelope theorem to the compatible table proves
\[
 \Theta_{T_1}(p^{\rm gain})
 =\left[-\frac7{10},\frac7{10}\right]
 \subsetneq
 \left[-\frac45,\frac45\right]
 =\Theta_{T_0}(p^{\rm gain}).
 \tag{15}
\]

Finally, the gain itself is perturbation-stable.  Set \(\eta_{\rm gain}=1/100\), and let \(p'\) be armwise normalized with
\(\lVert p'-p^{\rm gain}\rVert_\infty<\eta_{\rm gain}\).  Every cell exceeds \(9/100\), and the largest compatibility sum in (11) can increase by less than \(2/100\); hence it remains smaller than one.  The compatibility lemma therefore gives \(p'\in\mathcal P_{T_1}\).

All eight target cells lie in \((9/100,11/100)\).  Each cross cap entering \(u\) or \(v\) is larger than \(1-2(11/100)=78/100\).  Thus the individual caps are determined by the corresponding target-cell minima and satisfy
\[
 \frac9{100}<u(p'),v(p')<\frac{11}{100},
 \qquad
 \frac{18}{100}<D_{T_0}(p')<\frac{22}{100}.
 \tag{16}
\]
The nuisance caps satisfy
\[
 \frac8{100}<h_{c_\star0}(p')<\frac{12}{100},
 \qquad
 \frac{68}{100}<h_{c_\star1}(p')<\frac{72}{100}.
 \tag{17}
\]
Equations (16)--(17) show that \(D_{T_1}(p')=h_{c_\star0}(p')\), and hence
\[
 L_{T_1}(p')-L_{T_0}(p')
 =D_{T_0}(p')-D_{T_1}(p')>\frac6{100}.
 \tag{18}
\]
For \(\bar p'\), all target cells obey the same bounds, while
\[
 h_{c_\star1}(\bar p')=h_{c_\star0}(p').
\]
Repeating (16)--(18) for \(\bar p'\), and using \(U_S(p')=-L_S(\bar p')\), gives
\[
 U_{T_0}(p')-U_{T_1}(p')>\frac6{100}.
 \tag{19}
\]
The sharp-envelope theorem and (18)--(19) therefore yield
\[
 [L_{T_1}(p'),U_{T_1}(p')]
 \subsetneq [L_{T_0}(p'),U_{T_0}(p')]
\]
throughout this relative open neighborhood.  The argument uses, respectively, a finite restriction pushforward, an explicit response-law witness, a disjoint-event capacity inequality, and direct evaluation of the sharp affine endpoint functional; all positivity, normalization, compatibility, and strict-slack conditions used by those steps were verified above.

Write \(\Delta(\mathcal I)\) for the probability simplex on \(\mathcal I=\mathcal E\times\{0,1\}\).  Thus the observable conditional table is \(p=(p^0,p^1)\in\Delta(\mathcal I)^2\), and, under the positive-allocation condition used by the sharp-envelope theorem, the observable law is determined by \((\rho,p)\) through
\[
 \Pr_P(Z=z,X=x,Y=y)=\rho^z(1-\rho)^{1-z}p^z_{xy}.
\]
The causal identified set is
\[
 \Theta_T(p):=\{\mathbb E_q[V_b-V_a]:q\in\mathcal Q_T(p)\};
\]
it is not defined to equal an endpoint interval.

Because \(g\) is a wholly untrusted refinement, no trusted category is split.  More precisely, the definition of a wholly untrusted refinement supplies a bijection
\[
 \iota:T\longrightarrow\widetilde T
 \quad\text{such that}\quad
 g^{-1}(\{x\})=\{\iota(x)\}\quad(x\in T),
\]
whereas every element lying above \(U=\mathcal E\setminus T\) is untrusted.  The armwise push-forward condition therefore gives, for every \(x\in T\), \(y,z\in\{0,1\}\),
\[
 p^z_{xy}
 =\sum_{\widetilde x:g(\widetilde x)=x}
       \widetilde p^z_{\widetilde x y}
 =\widetilde p^z_{\iota(x)y}.                                      \tag{1}
\]
Aggregation preserves armwise normalization because
\[
 \sum_{x\in\mathcal E}\sum_{y=0}^1p^z_{xy}
 =\sum_{x\in\mathcal E}\sum_{y=0}^1
   \sum_{\widetilde x:g(\widetilde x)=x}
       \widetilde p^z_{\widetilde x y}
 =\sum_{\widetilde x\in\widetilde{\mathcal E}}
   \sum_{y=0}^1\widetilde p^z_{\widetilde x y}=1.                 \tag{2}
\]
Nonnegativity is also preserved term by term.  For each trusted cell, equation \((1)\) gives
\[
 p^0_{xy}+p^1_{x,1-y}
 =\widetilde p^0_{\iota(x)y}
  +\widetilde p^1_{\iota(x),1-y}.                                \tag{3}
\]
The map \(x\mapsto\iota(x)\) bijects the entire family of trusted compatibility inequalities on the right of \((3)\) with the corresponding family on the left.  The compatibility lemma, applied once on \(\mathcal E\) and once on \(\widetilde{\mathcal E}\), together with normalization and nonnegativity in \((2)\), now yields
\[
 \mathcal Q_{\widetilde T}(\widetilde p)\ne\varnothing
 \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
 \mathcal Q_T(p)\ne\varnothing.                                  \tag{4}
\]
This argument uses neither division nor strict positivity of any cell, so \((4)\) includes zero cells and equality in every compatibility inequality.

It remains to prove equality of the identifying functionals rather than stipulate it.  Put \(\widetilde a=\iota(a)\) and \(\widetilde b=\iota(b)\), and decorate endpoint components computed from \(\widetilde p\) with tildes.  Equation \((1)\), first for \(a\) and then for \(b\), implies for \(z\in\{0,1\}\)
\[
 \widetilde\alpha_z=\alpha_z,qquad
 \widetilde\gamma_z=\gamma_z,qquad
 \widetilde\beta_z=\beta_z,qquad
 \widetilde\delta_z=\delta_z.                                    \tag{5}
\]
Substitution in the definitions of \(\kappa\), \(u\), and \(v\) gives
\[
 \widetilde\kappa=\kappa,qquad
 \widetilde u=u,qquad
 \widetilde v=v.                                                   \tag{6}
\]
Moreover, \(c\mapsto\iota(c)\) is a bijection from \(T\setminus\{a,b\}\) to \(\widetilde T\setminus\{\widetilde a,\widetilde b\}\), and for each such \(c\) and each \(y\in\{0,1\}\), equation \((1)\) yields
\[
 \widetilde h_{\iota(c),y}
 =1-\widetilde p^0_{\iota(c)y}
    -\widetilde p^1_{\iota(c),1-y}
 =1-p^0_{cy}-p^1_{c,1-y}
 =h_{cy}.                                                          \tag{7}
\]
Consequently the two finite collections entering the minimum that defines the two-diagonal capacity are identical, including the case \(T=\{a,b\}\), when the collection consists only of \(u+v\).  Hence
\[
 D_{\widetilde T}(\widetilde p)
 =\min\!\left(\{\widetilde u+\widetilde v\}
       \cup\{\widetilde h_{\widetilde c y}:
               \widetilde c\in\widetilde T\setminus
                    \{\widetilde a,\widetilde b\},\ y\in\{0,1\}\}\right)
 =D_T(p).                                                          \tag{8}
\]
Equations \((6)\) and \((8)\), followed by the definition of the lower endpoint, prove
\[
 L_{\widetilde T}(\widetilde p)
 =\widetilde\kappa-D_{\widetilde T}(\widetilde p)
 =\kappa-D_T(p)
 =L_T(p).                                                          \tag{9}
\]

Outcome reversal commutes with push-forward: for every \(x,y,z\),
\[
 \sum_{\widetilde x:g(\widetilde x)=x}
      \overline{\widetilde p}^{,z}_{\widetilde x y}
 =\sum_{\widetilde x:g(\widetilde x)=x}
      \widetilde p^z_{\widetilde x,1-y}
 =p^z_{x,1-y}
 =\bar p^z_{xy}.                                                   \tag{10}
\]
Thus the already proved lower-endpoint argument applies to the pair \((\overline{\widetilde p},\bar p)\), and gives
\[
 L_{\widetilde T}(\overline{\widetilde p})=L_T(\bar p).
\]
Using the definition \(U_T(p)=-L_T(\bar p)\), we obtain
\[
 U_{\widetilde T}(\widetilde p)
 =-L_{\widetilde T}(\overline{\widetilde p})
 =-L_T(\bar p)
 =U_T(p).                                                          \tag{11}
\]

Finally suppose the equivalent compatibility conditions in \((4)\) hold.  The sharp-envelope theorem, applied to the coarse and refined models, identifies the causal sets as
\[
 \Theta_T(p)=[L_T(p),U_T(p)]
 \quad\text{and}\quad
 \Theta_{\widetilde T}(\widetilde p)
   =[L_{\widetilde T}(\widetilde p),U_{\widetilde T}(\widetilde p)].
\]
Equations \((9)\) and \((11)\) therefore prove
\[
 \Theta_{\widetilde T}(\widetilde p)=\Theta_T(p).
\]
This is sharp equality, not merely an outer bound, because the sharp-envelope theorem supplies endpoint-attaining response laws and mixtures attaining every interior point in each model.  Splitting a bin wholly inside \(U\) is exactly such a refinement, and merging those children is its push-forward comparison.  Hence either operation is target-ancillary, while no conclusion is asserted here for splitting a trusted category or declaring a refined child trusted.
